You receive 5 images. Image 1 is the LAYOUT SKETCH of the finished 1920x1080 game screen: a crude flat-colour blocking that fixes the exact composition - camera, horizon, wall and floor lines, and the position, size and outline of every object. Repaint image 1 into a finished painting: keep every line and every block exactly where it is and exactly as large as it is, paint each block as the object described below, do not move, enlarge, shrink, add or remove anything, and leave no flat colour areas or hard geometric edges. Images 2-4 are photos of the real place (geography, architecture, materials and real details to paint from; they are references only, do not copy their camera, cars, people, signs or weather). Image 5 is a finished background painting from our game: use it ONLY as the reference for the painting technique (brushwork, palette, edge softness, level of detail, line quality); do not copy anything from its scene.

Place: the Švantnerova tram stop on the Dúbravka - Karlova Ves tram line in Bratislava-Dúbravka, Slovakia: two side platforms with the double tram track in the green median of the wide M. Schneidra-Trnavského street, a low 1980s shopping pavilion across the street and the panel housing estate of Dúbravka around. Image 2 is a real photo taken on this platform (2022): concrete platform, the track with an incoming tram, low tube railings, traction poles. Image 3 is a real photo of the same stop from the street (2021): the platforms with railings and shelters, the shopping pavilion side. Image 4 is a real 1993 photo of the red-and-cream Tatra T6A5 tram of Bratislava: paint the tram exactly in this livery and shape. This scene is in June 1995, so paint the stop as it was then, not as in the 2021/2022 photos: original 1980s concrete-slab platforms, simple steel-and-glass shelters with paper posters, a paper timetable on a post, no electronic displays, no tactile paving, no modern shelters, no modern cars or shop logos.

Brief: a stylised tram stop by the housing estate on a warm sunny June morning in 1995 (15 June 1995): a red-and-cream tram without any line number, a paper timetable, an old typical street clock in a round brass frame that works as a time node, more colourful posters on the shelter than today. Morning light from the front right, warm and fresh, long soft shadows falling towards the viewer and to the left, a few green lime-tree leaves; same brushwork and palette as image 5.

Camera: seen from slightly above, as from about 3.5 m high over our platform, looking straight across the double track at the opposite platform; the tracks run horizontally across the picture; vertical lines stay vertical. Keep this exact geometry from the sketch: our platform from y 750 down to the bottom edge; the near track from y 602 to y 750 with its near rail exactly at y 680; the strip of ballast and short grass between the tracks at y 518-602; the far track at y 426-518; the far platform from its edge stones at y 412-426 back to a low green tube railing at y 248-256; behind it the far carriageway (y 172-248), a far pavement and a grass strip, and at the top edge the ground floor of the shopping pavilion.

What the sketch blocks are: at the top the ground floor of a low 1980s shopping pavilion with large shop windows and no signs, a grass strip with the trunks of young lime trees (their crowns above the frame), a pavement and the far carriageway with a dashed white lane line; the low green tube railing at the back of the far platform; the far platform paved with big worn concrete slabs; on its left a long simple 1980s tram shelter: a flat roof slab with a dark red steel fascia, dark red steel posts and a see-through glass back wall, with three colourful generic posters on its right part (bright shapes and colours only, no readable words, no brands); a concrete traction pole between the two tracks; the double tram track on concrete track panels with ballast and steel rails; on the right a red-and-cream Tatra T6A5 tram standing on the far track, its front facing left (big front windscreen, cream upper body with side windows, red lower front with two round headlights and a yellow coupler cover), with an empty black line-number box and a blank destination box - no numbers, no letters; our platform in front, paved with big light 1980s concrete slabs with a pale row of edge stones along the track; at its left end a lowered granite kerb flush with the paving, with a chipped corner at x 150, y 890, and a small asphalt footway beyond it at the far left edge; on the right, at the edge of our platform, a short dark green cast-iron column carrying the old street clock.
Fixed architectural anchor 'curb' at x 150, y 890. Fixed architectural anchor 'track_line' at x 960, y 680. Fixed architectural anchor 'clock_frame' at x 1560, y 320. The anchors must be painted exactly there: the chipped corner of the lowered kerb at the curb point, the near rail of the near track passing through the track_line point, and the centre of the round brass clock frame at the clock_frame point (the clock is about 110 px wide, white dial with black hour ticks and two hands, no numerals, a little worn brass frame).

Interactive props - each painted clearly inside its block, the same size as its block, easy to recognise at a glance:
1. the block of the layout sketch at x 120-240, y 150-250 of the 1920x1080 frame (6-12 % from the left, 14-23 % from the top): the glazed metal timetable case fixed to a grey stop post at the front edge of the far platform, holding a printed paper timetable (columns of tiny illegible print, no readable digits); above the block the small white tram-stop plate with a red border and a black tram pictogram, no words.
2. the block of the layout sketch at x 425-545, y 150-250 of the 1920x1080 frame (22-28 % from the left, 14-23 % from the top): inside the shelter, a weathered wooden slat bench on a steel frame with its backrest against the glass wall; a few old pink chewing-gum blobs stuck to the front edge and the underside of its seat.

Only the morning light, soft shadows and a few lime leaves. The platform continues to the left edge over the lowered kerb towards the school (the area of the layout sketch at x 50-105, y 975-1045 of the 1920x1080 frame (3-5 % from the left, 90-97 % from the top)), to the bottom edge towards the housing-estate yard (the area of the layout sketch at x 960-1015, y 975-1045 of the 1920x1080 frame (50-53 % from the left, 90-97 % from the top)) and to the right edge (the area of the layout sketch at x 1870-1925, y 975-1045 of the 1920x1080 frame (97-100 % from the left, 90-97 % from the top)).
